- "Even if the master of the Murim changed, the world itself would remain the same." — 무림의 주인이 바뀐다 해도 세상은 변함없을 것이다. Good. "master of the Murim" = owner of Murim. Fine.

- "There were villains in the orthodox faction and good people in the Demonic Cult." — 정파에도 악인은 있고, 마교에도 선인은 있다. Good.

- "Mae Jonghak was lost in thought for a long while before suddenly tapping his forehead." good. "이마를 탁 쳤더랬다" = slapped his forehead. "tapping" is lighter; "slapped his forehead" better. Change to "suddenly slapped his forehead."

- "“Oh, now that I think about it, you’re right.”" — 어, 생각해 보니 당신의 말이 맞구려. Good.

- "“That’s that, and this is this, isn’t it?”" good.

- "“What kind of nonsense is that? If you’re going to keep talking rubbish, go home.”" — 이게 무슨…… 헛소리할 거면 그만 돌아가시오. "헛소리" = nonsense/rubbish. Good. Hmm "go home" = 돌아가시오 (go back). "then just go back." Fine.

- "“Then let’s do this. We’ll follow the law of the Murim.”" good. 법도 = law/precepts. "the law of the Murim" fine.

- "“Might makes right?”" good.

- "“If I lose, I’ll leave without complaint. Not only that, I’ll keep your existence hidden from the Murim forever. However…”" — 불문에 부치지 = I will leave it unmentioned. "keep your existence hidden from the Murim forever." Good. Hmm "뿐만 아니라 영원히 당신의 존재를 불문에 부치지" = "moreover, I'll forever consign your existence to oblivion (never mention you)." Good.

- "“If you win, I have to help the orthodox Murim.”" good.

- "“Exactly. What do you say?”" good.

- "They fought for seven days and seven nights." good.

- "It was a battle between Huashan, which had taken root as a great tree of the Murim over hundreds of years, and the Fire Gate Clan, whose martial arts had been passed down according to the principles of one-man succession and secret transmission." Good. Maybe "a great tree rooted in the Murim for hundreds of years." Hmm. "which had put down roots as a towering tree of the Murim over hundreds of years." Baseline fine.

- "It was a bloody struggle between two Martial Gods." good.

- "“What a pity. With martial arts like yours, why are you holed up in a mountain village like this?”" good.

- "“Mind your own business. It’s my affair. What does it have to do with you?”" good.

- "“…Listening to you is exhausting. What are you going to do now?”" good. Hmm "기 빨리는군" literally "energy-draining." "Listening to you is exhausting." good. Or "You're exhausting to listen to." Keep.

- "“Honestly, I’d love to keep going, but… they crossed Gansu and Sichuan fifteen days ago. It’s a shame, but let’s leave it here this time.”" good.

- "It had been fortunate for Jeok Cheongang." good. Hmm "It was a stroke of luck for Jeok Cheongang." Keep.

- "Mae Jonghak was ten years younger than him, yet he was already an astonishingly powerful master." good. "at least ten years younger". Change to "at least ten years younger"? Korean "십 년은 젊었지만" = "younger by at least ten years". I'll add "at least". Good.

- "Without his own formidable internal energy, Jeok Cheongang would never have been able to endure." good.

- "“They may reach Anhui soon. Take care of yourself.”" good. Hmm, 안휘성 = Anhui province; glossary 안휘 = Anhui. "this place, Anhui" — the source "이곳, 안휘성으로" = "to this place, Anhui Province." Baseline "They may reach Anhui soon." Fine.

- "“No problem. All I have to do is guard Mount Jiuhua.”" good.

- "“Oh. That’s true.”" good.

- "“…Please stop talking and go.”" good.

- "The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak left just like that, and the Demonic Cult's army surged forward like a wave and crossed into Anhui." good.

- "Fifteen days later, the Demonic Cultists passing through Mount Jiuhua made a grave mistake." good.

- "“Set it on fire!”" good.

- "Mount Jiuhua burned, and Jeok Cheongang emerged into the world." good.

- "Not one of the thousand Demonic Cultists survived." good.

- "And people began calling him by another name." good.

- "“Then my grandfather…?”" good.

- "Fire King Jeok Cheongang merely smiled faintly instead of answering." good.

Now, a few things: The flashbacks in the source are rendered as indented quotes in Korean (the ‘...’ lines). Baseline rendered them as normal dialogue with curly quotes. That's consistent with project style (no special formatting). Good.

One issue: In the source, the flashback dialogue is set off with single quotation marks and paragraph breaks. Baseline just uses “...” in sequence. Fine.

Now consider the sfx "쐐애애애액! 쉭!" first occurrence: baseline "*Whooosh! Shhk!*". Then later "쐐애애애액!" alone → "*Whooosh!*" and "쉬쉬쉭!" → "*Shhk-shhk!*". Hmm, inconsistent: first "Shhk!" for 쉭, later "Shhk-shhk!" for 쉬쉬쉭 (two swishes). Fine.

Now "extreme" issues: none major.

Let me also double check "shisudaem": Actually, maybe better as "shisutem" nah. Keep.

Hmm, wait — one thing: the joke where Cheongpung says his grandfather told him "any man who hides behind someone else's name deserves to have his balls cut off." Then Jeok asks "네 사부가 누구냐?" and Cheongpung says "저희 할아버지요" ("My grandfather"). Jeok responds "말귀가 꽉 막힌 놈이로군. 네 할아비가 누구인지 노부가 어찌 알겠느냐?" = "You're a dense brat. How would I know who your grandpa is?" — wait, actually the joke: Jeok asked "who is your Master (사부)?" and Cheongpung answered "my grandfather." Jeok says "you dense brat, how would I know who your grandfather is?" meaning he wanted the name. Hmm, but actually Cheongpung then quotes his grandfather's saying rather than giving the name. Then Jeok laughs. Actually the flow: Jeok asks who his master is; Cheongpung says "my grandfather"; Jeok says "how would I know who your grandfather is" (i.e., give me a name); Cheongpung responds with the grandfather's quote about not hiding behind others' names — i.e., he won't name-drop. That's the joke! So Cheongpung refuses to name his grandfather, quoting him. Good — baseline preserves this.

Wait, the baseline: 
"“Who is your Master?”
“My grandfather.”
“What an obtuse brat. How would this old man know who your grandfather is?”
“My grandfather used to say that any man who hides behind someone else’s name after being born a man deserves to have his balls cut off.”"

Yes, preserves the joke. Good.

Now let me also verify "Three Saints"/삼성 etc. not in this chapter. Fine.

"삼성(三成)" here is 三成 = 30%, not the Three Saints 삼성. Baseline "three-tenths" correct. Good, the hanja in source is 三成. Good.

Now "극의에 다다른 열양지기" — baseline "Scorching Yang Qi that had reached the pinnacle". Good.

Now "he was using only three-tenths of his internal energy" — 삼성에 불과한 공력. Good.

Now, about "shisudaem" again — hmm. Let me also consider that in the Korean, 적천강 misheard Taekyung's "시스템". Rendering as "shisudaem" might be too obscure. But maybe rendering as "some 'shisutum' or other" is better? I'll keep baseline. Enough.

Hmm, actually, you know what — let me reconsider once more, because the brief says make it read like professional native English. "shisudaem" in the middle of an English sentence is jolting. But it's deliberate—the character is quoting a weird foreign word. It might be fine with quotes. Actually maybe clearer to write it as a mangled English word: "some 'sis-tem' or other". Hmm, that reveals the mangle. The reader knows the System is called System, so seeing "sis-tem" they'd get it. I think that's actually the better editorial choice. But is changing the rendering allowed? "Do not replace an established rendering... with a synonym merely because the synonym sounds smoother." Hmm, this is a transliteration choice, not an established glossary term. The baseline is accepted. I think keeping is safest. But professionalism...

Let me keep "shisudaem" — it's a transliteration of the Korean distortion, and the project seems to favor transliteration (e.g., "gongcheong seokyu"). Fine. Actually hmm, "gongcheong seokyu" is a transliteration of a Korean reading of Chinese characters. So transliteration is in-style. Keep "shisudaem".

Hmm, but wait: "System" is an English word; the Korean 시스템 is a loanword. Transliterating a mangled loanword of an English word back into English is weird (shisudaem ≈ "System" mangled). The natural English approach: show the mangle in English: "some 'Sis-tem' or whatever." I'm torn. 

I'll go with a compromise: "spouting incomprehensible nonsense about some 'shisudaem' or whatever." Keep. Final. (Decided.)

Hmm, actually let me reconsider what serves the reader. The line's function: Jeok Cheongang thinks Taekyung has been spouting gibberish about some nonsense word. The exact word doesn't matter much; the function is "unintelligible gibberish." "shisudaem" conveys unintelligibility perfectly (reader also goes "huh?"). That mirrors Jeok's experience! So it actually works thematically. Keep.

Now, let me reconsider a couple of lines for naturalness:

- "Jeok Cheongang had no particular hobby of tormenting children, but this one needed to be taught a lesson." — "no particular hobby of tormenting children" is a bit odd; "He didn't particularly enjoy tormenting children, but this one needed a lesson." Hmm. "취미는 없지만" = "he had no hobby of ~". Baseline's phrasing is fine and a bit funny. Keep? "had no particular hobby of tormenting children" – okay. Maybe "He took no particular pleasure in tormenting children, but this one needed to be taken down a peg." Hmm, "혼쭐이 나야 한다" = needs to be taught a lesson / get a scolding. "needed to be taught a lesson" good. I'll keep baseline but maybe reword slightly: "Jeok Cheongang had no particular taste for tormenting children, but this one needed to be knocked down a peg." Hmm "knocked down a peg" changes image. Keep "taught a lesson".

Keep baseline mostly.

- "It was hard to listen to." — perhaps "It was unbearable to listen to." Hmm, 듣고 있기 힘들었다 = hard to keep listening. Baseline fine.

Now, let me make sure the chapter heading is `# Chapter 172`. Yes.

Also should I keep "Murim" with capital letter.

Now finalize edits. Let me produce the final chapter with the noted improvements:

1. "Unlike Hyuk Mujin..." keep.
2. "Instead of blood spraying before his eyes..." → recast.
3. "Cheongpung licked his lips" → "smacked his lips".
4. "stood frozen like a monument" → "like a statue".
5. "heated to a reddish hue" → "gone red all over".
6. "while you bully my Benefactor, sir?" → "Grandpa".
7. "That meant Cheongpung had grown up around someone who stood at the same realm stage as him." → polish.
8. "obtuse brat" → "dense brat".
9. "A palm strike struck him in the chest" → "A palm slammed into his chest".
10. "suddenly tapping his forehead" → "suddenly slapped his forehead".
11. "ten years younger" → "at least ten years younger".

Let me also reconsider #6 more. Hmm, is "Grandpa" going to read well? "How could I just stand by while you bully my Benefactor, Grandpa?" Hmm. Wait, it might momentarily read as if Cheongpung's own grandfather is doing the bullying, since he then asks "Are you going to kill me?" Hmm. Actually Cheongpung says 할아버지 meaning the old man he's addressing. If I write ", Grandpa?" it's clear he's addressing him. Hmm, but it could confuse since his real grandfather is Mae Jonghak and there's a later reveal... Actually that confusion is present in the Korean too (he addresses Jeok as 할아버지, and later mentions his actual 할아버지). So it's source-faithful. Keep "Grandpa".

Hmm, wait, but actually the confusion might be greater in English because "Grandpa" as a standalone address is less common. Meh. Alternative: "Grandpa Jeok"? No, he doesn't know the name yet? Actually he might; Jeok introduced himself? In ch171, Jeok Cheongang's name... Cheongpung might know. The table says he later uses 적 할아버지. But here plain 할아버지. So use "Grandpa". Hmm, but to avoid confusion, maybe put "grandfather" as the address: "How could I just stand by while you, grandpa, bully my Benefactor?" no.

Hmm, alternatively render as "sir" to avoid confusion, matching baseline. Ugh.

Let me think about which a professional editor would choose. The Korean uses a kinship address that's warm but polite. In English commercial fiction translation, "sir" is the standard neutralization, but the project seems to prefer preserving kinship ("Grandpa" used in ch170 for the old man talking to Hanga — though that's from the child). Given the project's established use of "Grandpa Jeok" for 적 할아버지, I'll preserve "Grandpa" here. Actually hold on, the table says Cheongpung uses 적 할아버지 — "Grandpa Jeok". If that's the established rendering, then plain 할아버지 → "Grandpa". Yes, consistent. Go with "Grandpa".

Hmm, but where's the 적 할아버지 line? Possibly in ch171? Let me check ch171 tail... no. It might be in a later chapter's matched pairs that got included? The packet's matched pairs are "for this Korean chapter", so all pairs should be from ch172. But I don't see 적 할아버지 in the source. Hmm. Let me search the source for 할아버지: 
- "저희 할아버지요." (my grandfather)
- "네 할아비가 누구인지" (your grandpa)
- "할아버지가 말씀하시길" (My grandfather said)
- "할아버지께서 제 은인을 핍박하는데"
- "우리 할아버지를"
- "우리 할아버지를 아세요?"
- "그럼 할아버지께서……?"

So no 적 할아버지. The matched pair entry mentions "적 할아버지 while asking Jeok Cheongang to confirm Taekyung's condition" — that must be from a different chapter (the packet's address table may span the arc). Hmm. Anyway, it establishes "Grandpa Jeok" as the project rendering for Cheongpung→Jeok. So plain 할아버지 here → "Grandpa". Good, consistent.

But hmm, in the line "할아버지께서 제 은인을 핍박하는데" the subject is "Grandpa" — so "while Grandpa oppresses my Benefactor". Hmm, actually that would be third person-ish? In Korean, using 할아버지께서 as subject to the person's face is normal polite/humble (like "Grandfather is..."). In English, "while you bully" is more natural. But to keep the address, "..., Grandpa" at the end works. I'll do that.

Final: "I owe that gentleman a bit. How could I just stand by while you bully my Benefactor, Grandpa?"

Hmm, "that gentleman" for 저분 — good.

OK.

Now #7: "That meant Cheongpung had grown up around someone who stood at the same realm stage as him." Rewrite: "That meant Cheongpung had grown up beside a master of that same realm stage." Good.

Now #2: "Instead of blood spraying before his eyes, Jeok Cheongang's figure scattered like mist." → "Instead of blood, Jeok Cheongang's figure scattered like mist before his eyes." Hmm. Or "Rather than blood, it was Jeok Cheongang's figure scattering like mist that met his eyes." Hmm. Let me do: "Instead of blood spurting, Jeok Cheongang's figure scattered like mist." Good. Actually source: "그의 눈앞에 피를 뿌리는 대신 안개처럼 흩어지는 적천강의 신형이 보였다." = "Before his eyes, instead of spraying blood, he saw Jeok Cheongang's form scattering like mist." So: "Instead of spraying blood, Jeok Cheongang's form dissolved like mist before his eyes." I'll use that.

Hmm "신형" = figure/form. "form" fine.

Now #5: "Hot steam rose in wisps from his entire body, which had been heated to a reddish hue." → "Hot steam rose in wisps from his body, which had gone red all over." Good.

Wait, source: "온통 불그스름하게 달아오른 그의 전신에서 뜨거운 김이 모락모락 솟아나고 있었다." = "From his whole body, flushed reddish all over, hot steam was rising in wisps." So order: body flushed red; steam rising. Baseline has it as relative clause. Fine. Maybe reorder: "His whole body had flushed a reddish hue, and hot steam rose from it in wisps." That's natural. But "his entire body" — the subject of the paragraph is Taekyung (pointed at). "His whole body had flushed red, hot steam rising from it in wisps." Nice. I'll use: "His whole body had flushed a feverish red, and hot steam rose from it in wisps." Hmm "feverish" adds. Just "red". Use "His whole body had flushed red, and hot steam rose from it in wisps."

Now other potential improvements:

- "The corner of his wrinkled mouth rose slightly." → "The corner of his wrinkled mouth curled up slightly." Minor. I'll change to "curled up".

- "Come." keep.

- "“Uh… Returning to Simplicity and Shifting Form and Position… We seem to have picked the wrong fight.”" Hmm, "단단히 잘못 걸린 것 같은데요" = "I think we've gotten ourselves into serious trouble." "We seem to have picked the wrong fight" is fine. Maybe "We really seem to have picked the wrong opponent." Hmm. Keep baseline.

- "Your eyes are pretty useful." — 눈깔 = crude "eyeballs". "Your eyes are pretty sharp." Hmm, "쓸 만하구나" = "quite usable." "Your eyes are pretty useful" preserves. Keep.

- "I've seen a lot of things since I was little." Hmm, "어렸을 때부터 많이 보고 자랐거든요" = "I grew up seeing a lot of it." Baseline fine.

- "You grew up watching?" — good.

- "Can you bear the punishment for daring to point a sword at this old man?" good.

- "Would it have made a difference if you had?" good.

- "He did not know which sect or master the boy belonged to" — "어디 문하의 누구인지는 모르겠지만" = "he didn't know whose disciple he was". Fine.

- "There was something in them that some people called reckless bravado and others called chivalry." Keep.

- "“This is the Murim. Should this old man take circumstances like that into account?”" good.

- "“His courage was admirable. Get some rest.”" Hmm "용기는 가상했다" = "your courage was admirable/commendable". "그만 쉬어라" = "take a rest now". Good.

- "More importantly…" — 그건 그렇고 = "anyway, that aside". "More importantly" changes nuance slightly ("그건 그렇고" = "that aside"). Hmm. "Anyway…" Hmm but then the next is Jeok glancing at the blade. "That aside…" Let me use "That aside…". Hmm, "그건 그렇고" is a transition meaning "anyway" / "setting that aside." Baseline "More importantly…" is acceptable but slightly different. I'll change to "That aside…". Hmm, "Anyway…" reads more natural in dialogue. Use "Anyway…". Hmm.

Actually, I'll use "That aside…" — it's clean and accurate. Hmm, but Jeok is an old-school speaker; "That aside…" fits. Use it.

- "Zaha Divine Technique. Are you a disciple of Huashan?" good.

- "Cheongpung answered by throwing a punch." good.

- "Jeok Cheongang dredged up a memory from long ago." good.

- "The next moment, the Sword Energy narrowly missed Jeok Cheongang and reduced the surrounding area to ruins." good.

- "Cheongpung swallowed a mouthful of thickly rising dust and coughed." good.

- "It had been more than forty years ago." keep.

- "That was when the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak visited Mount Jiuhua." keep.

- "Those were his first words." keep.

- "Jeok Cheongang was surprised by the visit of a master who could be compared to himself, but his answer had already been decided." keep. ("난생 처음" = for the first time in his life — dropped. Could add "for the first time in his life." Hmm: "Jeok Cheongang was surprised—for the first time in his life—by the visit of a master who could be compared to himself." Adds fidelity. I'll include.)

Hmm, "난생 처음 ... 놀랐지만" = "was surprised as never before." I'll render "It was the first time in his life he had been visited by a master who could be compared to himself, and it surprised him; but his answer was already decided." Hmm wordy. Better: "Jeok Cheongang was startled by the visit of a master who could stand beside him—the first such in his life—but his answer had already been decided." Hmm. Let me do: "A master who could be compared to himself had come to visit—the first in his life—and Jeok Cheongang was surprised, but his answer had already been decided." Hmm. I'll go with: "It was the first time in his life that a master comparable to himself had come calling, and Jeok Cheongang was surprised. But his answer was already decided." Good.

- "“Let’s speak plainly. It’s your orthodox Murim that’s in danger, not the world.”" good.

- "Even if the master of the Murim changed, the world itself would remain the same." good. Maybe "Even if the Murim changed hands, the world would remain the same." Hmm, "무림의 주인이 바뀐다 해도" = "even if the owner of the Murim changed." "Even if the Murim changed hands" is natural. Use that? It's a nice idiom. But "주인" = master/owner. "Even if the Murim changed hands" is a good idiomatic rendering. I'll use it.

- "There were villains in the orthodox faction and good people in the Demonic Cult." good.

- "And Jeok Cheongang intended to remain on Mount Jiuhua forever." good.

- "Mae Jonghak was lost in thought for a long while before suddenly slapping his forehead." good.

- "“What kind of nonsense is that? If you’re going to keep talking rubbish, go home.”" good.

- "“Then let’s do this. We’ll follow the law of the Murim.”" good.

- "“If I lose, I’ll leave without complaint. Not only that, I’ll keep your existence hidden from the Murim forever. However…”" good.

- "They fought for seven days and seven nights." good.

- "It was a battle between Huashan, which had taken root as a great tree of the Murim over hundreds of years, and the Fire Gate Clan, whose martial arts had been passed down according to the principles of one-man succession and secret transmission." good.

Hmm "일인전승 비인부전" – "one-man succession, not transmitted to two" — "one-man succession and secret transmission" hmm "비인부전" = "not passed to a second person". "secret transmission" approximates. Fine.

- "It was a bloody struggle between two Martial Gods." good.

- "“What a pity. With martial arts like yours, why are you holed up in a mountain village like this?”" good.

- "“Mind your own business. It’s my affair. What does it have to do with you?”" good.

- "“Oh. Now that I think about it, you’re right.”" good.

- "“Honestly, I’d love to keep going, but… they crossed Gansu and Sichuan fifteen days ago. It’s a shame, but let’s leave it here this time.”" good.

- "It had been fortunate for Jeok Cheongang." good. Hmm maybe "As it happened, that was lucky for Jeok Cheongang." Keep.

- "Mae Jonghak was at least ten years younger than him, yet he was already an astonishingly powerful master." good.

- "And people began calling him by another name." good.

- "Fire King Jeok Cheongang merely smiled faintly instead of answering." good.

I think the baseline is very good. Let me now write the final version with my tweaks.

Let me also double-check the "shisudaem" sentence: baseline "All this time, the boy had been spouting incomprehensible nonsense about some “shisudaem” or whatever. It was hard to listen to." Maybe combine: "From earlier, the boy had been spouting incomprehensible nonsense about some 'shisudaem' or whatever, and he could hardly stand to listen." Hmm, "아까부터" = "since a while ago." Baseline "All this time". Fine. Keep.

One more: the opening "*Heh heh. Have a taste of something hot, you little punk.*" — good.

Now double-check "Scorching Yang Qi that had reached the pinnacle" — maybe "Scorching Yang Qi honed to its absolute limit." Hmm, 극의에 다다른 = "that had reached the extreme/utmost." Fine.

Also "his fingertips carried" — 손가락 끝에는 ... 실려 있었다. "his fingertips bore". Fine.

Now about "Hk!" for 흐읍 — maybe "Hnngh!" Hmm. "Hk!" is fine. Could be "Huff!" Hmm. Keep.

Alright, also the System panels: none in this chapter.

Final check on formatting: curly quotes, italics for thoughts, em dashes without spaces (baseline uses "—"), ellipsis character "…". Baseline uses "…" good. The source has "……" (double) rendered as "…" mostly. Fine.

Let me write it out.

Wait, one more: "Mae Jonghak—what is your relationship with that friend of mine?" Hmm the source "매종학, 그 친구와는 어떤 관계냐?" Actually maybe render "Mae Jonghak, is he...? What is your relationship with that fellow?" Hmm. Keep.

Also "Cheongpung felt as though he were facing his grandfather, the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak." — note: source names 검성 매종학 = Sword Saint. Good.

Let me write final.

Also decide: "“No problem. All I have to do is guard Mount Jiuhua.”" — 일 없소. "No trouble." Keep.

Now let me produce the output. No commentary, just the chapter.

Actually, one more consideration on "차원이 다르다": baseline "The difference in their levels was absolute." I'll rewrite as "They were on a completely different level." Hmm, or keep. The line stands alone as a punchy beat. "The gap between them was absolute." I like: "The gap between them was absolute." Actually "차원이 다르다" literally "the dimension is different". "They were on a different plane." Hmm. I'll use "They were on a completely different level." Simple.

Writing now.

# Chapter 172

Jeok Cheongang wore a smug grin.

*Heh heh. Have a taste of something hot, you little punk.*

His fingertips carried Scorching Yang Qi that had reached the pinnacle.

Though he was using only three-tenths of his internal energy, it was still far beyond what a fledgling who looked barely twenty could withstand.

*This ought to snap him back to his senses.*

Jeok Cheongang had no particular hobby of tormenting children, but this one needed to be taught a lesson.

All this time, the boy had been spouting incomprehensible nonsense about some “shisudaem” or whatever. It was hard to listen to.

*I’ve controlled my strength, so if things go well, he might even avoid an Internal Injury.*

If things went well.

Jeok Cheongang added that condition silently as he reached out.

*Tap.*

The instant his bony, wrinkled finger touched the young man’s broad chest, Extreme Yang Qi surged forward like a tidal wave. Jin Taekyung sucked in a startled breath.

“Hk!”

“How is it? Feels like there’s a fire burning inside you, doesn’t it?”

Jeok Cheongang could not help laughing when he saw the boy’s face turn bright red. The saying that a beating was the best medicine truly was an eternal truth.

“Now, stop talking nonsense and tell me the truth—”

*Whooosh! Shhk!*

Jeok Cheongang could not finish his sentence. Two swords had flashed in like lightning and slashed through his waist and arm.

“Did it work? It worked! Young Hero Cheong, you did it!”

Unlike Hyuk Mujin, who was celebrating with a dazed expression, Cheongpung merely scratched the back of his head.

Instead of spraying blood, Jeok Cheongang’s form dissolved like mist before his eyes.

“Uh… Returning to Simplicity and Shifting Form and Position… We seem to have picked the wrong fight.”

Jeok Cheongang was already sitting on a fence some distance away, laughing loudly.

“Your eyes are pretty useful.”

“I’ve seen a lot of things since I was little.”

“You grew up watching?”

Jeok Cheongang was genuinely surprised when he realized what those words implied.

Returning to Simplicity and Shifting Form and Position were both domains permitted only to Supreme Peak masters. That meant Cheongpung had grown up beside a master of that same realm stage.

“Who is your Master?”

“My grandfather.”

“What a dense brat. How would this old man know who your grandfather is?”

“My grandfather used to say that any man who hides behind someone else’s name after being born a man deserves to have his balls cut off.”

“Ha ha ha! What a splendid saying!”

After bursting into laughter, Jeok Cheongang fixed Cheongpung with a long look.

“Can you bear the punishment for daring to point a sword at this old man?”

Cheongpung smacked his lips, looking troubled.

“But I didn’t use Sword Energy. Couldn’t you let it slide?”

“Would it have made a difference if you had?”

“Hmm. I don’t think so.”

Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh. He did not know which sect or master the boy belonged to, but he was certainly an interesting one.

“Then why did you step forward?”

Cheongpung pointed at Jin Taekyung, who stood frozen like a statue.

His whole body had flushed red, and hot steam rose from it in wisps.

“I owe that gentleman a bit. How could I just stand by while you bully my Benefactor, Grandpa?”

“You must owe him quite a lot. Enough to risk your life, at least.”

Cheongpung’s eyes widened.

“Are you going to kill me?”

Of course, Jeok Cheongang had no intention of killing anyone here. But he deliberately hardened his expression and lowered his voice.

“Of course.”

“Uh-oh. That won’t do. There are still so many things I haven’t tried.”

“This is the Murim. Should this old man take circumstances like that into account?”

Cheongpung thought about it carefully before answering.

“I suppose not.”

Hyuk Mujin, who had been listening to their conversation with growing anxiety, suddenly exploded.

“You can’t just accept that, you idiot!”

“Why not?”

“Because that old man—no, that gentleman—is going to kill us!”

“He isn’t wrong. Hmm, and besides…”

Cheongpung calmly added,

“We won’t know whether we die or live until we try.”

“…Damn it. Fine, let’s do it. If we just sit here, Captain will beat us to death later anyway, so whatever.”

Jeok Cheongang rested his chin on his hand and gazed at the two young men.

They really were interesting.

One was willing to stake his life because he owed someone a debt. The other grumbled while stepping into a battle whose outcome was obvious.

There was something in them that some people called reckless bravado and others called chivalry.

*People like this always die young.*

That had been true forty years ago, and it would probably be true now as well.

That was why Jeok Cheongang had developed a faint fondness for the youngsters. At the very least, they possessed the courage to risk their lives for someone else.

Just as they were doing now.

“Then shall I teach you a thing or two?”

Jeok Cheongang slowly rose to his feet.

At the same time, an aura as vast as a mountain erupted from his short frame and pressed down on everything around him.

Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin gripped their sword hilts, while Jang Taebo collapsed onto the ground with a deathly white face.

“You stay out of this.”

Jeok Cheongang flicked a finger.

Jang Taebo’s body floated over the fence as though an invisible hand had seized and lifted him.

Cheongpung muttered at the sight,

“Seizing an object through empty space…”

With a single gesture, the old man had lifted Jang Taebo, whose body was larger than that of most full-grown men.

It was proof that the old man before them possessed internal energy no weaker than his grandfather’s.

Hyuk Mujin also muttered with a vacant expression,

“Damn. That’s something you only ever see in novels.”

They were on a completely different level.

At this moment, everything surrounding Jeok Cheongang was both his weapon and his shield. The corner of his wrinkled mouth curled up slightly.

“Come.”

That was the signal.

Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin charged with every ounce of strength they possessed.

The two knew each other’s martial arts intimately after countless duels. Their swords meshed perfectly as they unleashed a coordinated attack.

*Whooosh!*

*Shhk-shhk!*

Just as the two blades were about to pierce Jeok Cheongang’s flank and neck, he stretched out both hands.

His hands were suddenly engulfed in white flames as he caught the blades.

“Do you think that will be enough?”

*Grrrk.*

Hyuk Mujin’s eyes opened wide.

His beloved sword, forged from Baekryeon Jeonggang—the hardest steel imaginable—was bending. Then it turned into molten metal and began dripping away.

“What is this?”

He had put everything he had into that strike, yet he had not even managed to leave a scratch.

As he stared blankly at the blade, already half melted, Jeok Cheongang’s voice reached his ears.

“Your courage was admirable. Get some rest.”

The next moment, Hyuk Mujin’s vision turned white. A palm slammed into his chest, and he dropped helplessly to his knees.

“Young Hero Hyuk!”

“Don’t worry. He should have suffered no more than a minor Internal Injury. That aside…”

Jeok Cheongang glanced at the blade held in his other hand.

It had neither bent nor melted. Instead, it was wrapped in a faint purple Sword Energy.

Jeok Cheongang dredged up a memory from long ago.

“Zaha Divine Technique. Are you a disciple of Huashan?”

Cheongpung answered by throwing a punch.

The Crouching Tiger Fist, a powerful fist technique said to subdue tigers, slammed into Jeok Cheongang’s chest.

*Thud!*

Jeok Cheongang’s white eyebrows curved like a crescent moon.

“Well, look at you.”

That attack would have been enough to shatter a person’s chest, yet that was the entirety of his reaction.

Cheongpung felt as though he were facing his grandfather, the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.

*He’s strong. Overwhelmingly strong.*

But Cheongpung could not give up like this.

He exhaled slowly and stamped his foot into the ground. The Zaha Divine Technique’s energy rippling through his body flared even more fiercely.

“Go on, then. Let yourself run wild.”

Jeok Cheongang grinned and relaxed his grip on the blade.

Freed from its restraint, the sword unleashed the ultimate techniques of the Plum Blossom Sword Technique.

*Shiiiiing!*

The tip of the sword moved fluidly, drawing plum blossoms in the air.

One became two. Two became five. Five became nine…

At last, twenty-four fully formed plum blossoms transformed into streaks of light and poured down toward Jeok Cheongang.

At this moment, even Jeok Cheongang could not help feeling genuinely impressed.

*Huashan has produced an incredible talent.*

And that brought one person to mind.

A figure who was practically synonymous with Huashan.

No—a figure revered by every swordsman under heaven.

“Mae Jonghak—what is your relationship with that friend of mine?”

The twenty-four plum blossoms wavered dangerously at the word *friend*.

The next moment, the Sword Energy narrowly missed Jeok Cheongang and reduced the surrounding area to ruins.

*Kaboom!*

Cheongpung swallowed a mouthful of thickly rising dust and coughed.

“Cough, cough. Do you know my grandfather, cough?”

Jeok Cheongang laughed with evident pleasure.

“I’ve met him. A very long time ago.”

It had been more than forty years ago.

The Demonic Cult’s hundred thousand followers had devoured half the world. As the tide of war turned against the orthodox faction, the orthodox Murim began searching even for eccentric masters who had withdrawn into remote mountain valleys.

That was when the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak visited Mount Jiuhua.

“Help me.”

Those were his first words.

It was the first time in his life that a master comparable to himself had come calling, and Jeok Cheongang was surprised. But his answer was already decided.

“No.”

“The world is in danger.”

“Let’s speak plainly. It’s your orthodox Murim that’s in danger, not the world.”

Even if the Murim changed hands, the world itself would remain the same. There were villains in the orthodox faction and good people in the Demonic Cult.

And Jeok Cheongang intended to remain on Mount Jiuhua forever.

Mae Jonghak was lost in thought for a long while before suddenly slapping his forehead.

“Oh, now that I think about it, you’re right.”

“…You didn’t come here to persuade me?”

“That’s that, and this is this, isn’t it?”

“What kind of nonsense is that? If you’re going to keep talking rubbish, go home.”

“Then let’s do this. We’ll follow the law of the Murim.”

“Might makes right?”

“If I lose, I’ll leave without complaint. Not only that, I’ll keep your existence hidden from the Murim forever. However…”

“If you win, I have to help the orthodox Murim.”

“Exactly. What do you say?”

“Draw your sword.”

They fought for seven days and seven nights.

It was a battle between Huashan, which had taken root as a great tree of the Murim over hundreds of years, and the Fire Gate Clan, whose martial arts had been passed down according to the principles of one-man succession and secret transmission.

It was a bloody struggle between two Martial Gods.

And the result was a draw, with neither victor nor loser.

“What a pity. With martial arts like yours, why are you holed up in a mountain village like this?”

“Mind your own business. It’s my affair. What does it have to do with you?”

“Oh. Now that I think about it, you’re right.”

“…Listening to you is exhausting. What are you going to do now?”

“Honestly, I’d love to keep going, but… they crossed Gansu and Sichuan fifteen days ago. It’s a shame, but let’s leave it here this time.”

It had been fortunate for Jeok Cheongang.

If their battle had continued for even a few more days, he would have been the one to lose.

Mae Jonghak was at least ten years younger than him, yet he was already an astonishingly powerful master.

Without his own formidable internal energy, Jeok Cheongang would never have been able to endure.

“They may reach Anhui soon. Take care of yourself.”

“No problem. All I have to do is guard Mount Jiuhua.”

“Oh. That’s true.”

“…Please stop talking and go.”

The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak left just like that, and the Demonic Cult’s army surged forward like a wave and crossed into Anhui.

Fifteen days later, the Demonic Cultists passing through Mount Jiuhua made a grave mistake.

“Set it on fire!”

Mount Jiuhua burned, and Jeok Cheongang emerged into the world.

Not one of the thousand Demonic Cultists survived.

And people began calling him by another name.

“Then my grandfather…?”

Fire King Jeok Cheongang merely smiled faintly instead of answering.
